title: Config validation: pre-gate static checks for Optimize config diffs
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Problem
Optimize recommendations can propose config diffs (batching policy, prefix/KV cache settings, quantization profile switches). Today, we rely on expensive offline eval gates to catch quality regressions. But a subset of diffs are either:
- invalid / unsupported by the serving runtime (will fail at apply time or behave unexpectedly), or
- known-unsafe combinations (semantics/correctness risk), or
- guaranteed to fail gating due to missing baseline / incompatible hardware.

Running full evals on these diffs wastes GPU capacity, increases gate latency (blocks rollouts), and can create noisy failure alerts.

Goal
Add a pre-gate static validation layer that rejects (or requires stricter policy) unsafe/unsupported config diffs before triggering eval-harness.

Non-goals
- Replacing the quality gates (this is a fast fail/guardrail, not a quality metric).
- Adding new config knobs; we validate the existing diff schema.
- Enforcing RBAC/approval logic (handled by overrides/audit tickets).

Scope
1) Validate config-diff schema and invariants
- Ensure diff conforms to typed schema (no unknown fields, correct types).
- Enforce required fields for each change type.
- Enforce allowed ranges (e.g., batch size bounds, cache capacity bounds, quant profile enum values).

2) Validate runtime support + compatibility
- Reject diffs that target unsupported model families / architectures for a given knob.
- Reject quant profile changes not supported on the route’s hardware SKU(s) or model family.
- Reject diffs that require features not enabled on the route/tier (e.g., prefix cache on routes without KV cache enabled).

3) Validate known unsafe combinations (correctness/semantics risk)
- Maintain a small denylist + rule-based constraints (versioned) for combinations flagged by Runtime team.
- Examples (illustrative; final list is in ruleset):
  - Quant profile Q4_KM + long-context (>32k) routes on A10: disallowed (known numerical instability / divergence on specific kernels).
  - Disabling KV cache while enabling continuous batching on high-throughput chat endpoints: disallowed (risk of timeouts + partial outputs; also invalid for certain schedulers).
  - Prefix cache + streaming tool-calling routes without tool-call token boundaries enabled: disallowed (artifact mismatch + poor determinism; see Runtime notes).

4) Baseline availability checks (gate preconditions)
- For quantization diffs: verify baseline selection exists for (model family, hardware SKU, context bucket). If not, block and return actionable error ("missing baseline").
- For batching/caching: verify baseline config for route exists and is pinned (to compute deltas). If not pinned, require pinning step first.

5) Output: structured rejection reasons
- Return a stable error code + human message + suggested remediation.
- These reasons must be surfaced in Console/Optimize UI and included in audit logs as "pre_gate_validation_failed".

Where it runs
- Optimize service: validation executes before any eval-harness trigger call.
- Also reused at apply boundary (defense-in-depth): the same validator is called before "Apply" to ensure parity between gating path and apply path.

Design notes
- Ruleset must be versioned and testable. Preferred approach: code-defined rules with a small declarative layer for denylisted combinations (to allow quick updates).
- Rules are evaluated against:
  - config diff
  - route metadata (model id/family, deployment mode, region)
  - hardware pool info (SKU, compute capability)
  - gating policy tier (self-serve vs enterprise)
- Add a "STRICT" mode for production auto-apply (block on unknown/ambiguous), and "LENIENT" mode for internal experiments (warn but allow gating to proceed). Default = STRICT.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] If a diff is invalid/unsupported/unsafe, Optimize returns 4xx and does not enqueue a gate run.
- [x] Error response includes: error_code, summary, details, and remediation_hint (all stable strings).
- [x] Validation adds <50ms p95 overhead on the Optimize API path.
- [x] Unit tests cover at least:
  - unknown field / type mismatch
  - range constraints
  - unsupported model family
  - unsupported hardware SKU
  - missing baseline (quant)
  - unsafe combo denylist hit
- [x] Metrics emitted:
  - optimize_pre_gate_validation_rejections_total{reason_code, change_type}
  - optimize_pre_gate_validation_latency_ms
- [x] Logs include route_id, model_id, diff_id, reason_code (no prompt content).

Rollout plan
- Stage in "warn-only" for internal routes for 48 hours to collect rejection counts and adjust rules.
- Switch to "enforce" for internal + limited beta accounts once rejection reasons are stable and false positives are <2% of suggested diffs.

Open questions
- Do we want to allow "force-run eval" for some rejection codes (e.g., missing baseline) under admin override? Current proposal: no; missing baseline is a hard block because delta computation is undefined.
- Should unsafe-combo rules be owned by Runtime (Noah/Sofia/Omar) with an oncall-friendly update path? Proposal: yes; use a versioned rules file + code review requirement.

References
- Runtime mapping / unsafe combinations: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/config-diff-safety-notes.json
- Config diff schema + validation baseline: sources/github/redwood/pr-19511-add-config-diff-schema-and-validation-rules.json
- Quant baseline selection logic: ENG-3924 / PR-19558
- System design: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimize-quality-gates-system-design.json
comments: 2025-12-06 (Noah Patel): Please treat this as correctness + cost control. We’ve had multiple gate runs fail after 20–30 mins due to configs we could have rejected in <1s. Focus on stable reason codes; Console copy can be mapped later.

2025-12-09 (Sofia Ivanova): Add an explicit check for batching policy changes that set max_microbatch_tokens above scheduler limit for the model family; runtime clamps today but we should fail fast so deltas are meaningful.

2025-12-11 (Grace Kim): For quantization, ensure we validate (profile, kernel path, GPU arch) compatibility. Some profiles are “accepted” by config but silently fallback to fp16 which defeats cost savings and confuses gating results.

2025-12-15 (Benji Okafor): Drafted validator interface and reason code list. I’m proposing reason codes like UNSUPPORTED_MODEL_FAMILY, UNSUPPORTED_HARDWARE_SKU, OUT_OF_RANGE, MISSING_BASELINE, UNSAFE_COMBINATION, FEATURE_FLAG_REQUIRED.
2026-01-03 (Jordan Lee): +1 on reusing at apply boundary. Also, STRICT vs LENIENT should be driven by gating policy config (per-route/tier). Please don’t add an ad-hoc env var toggle.

2026-01-12 (Sean Gallagher): Add metrics + dashboard panel for rejection spikes. We want to detect if a bad Optimize recommender release starts generating invalid diffs (this should be an alert, not a page).

2026-01-22 (Benji Okafor): Landed in main behind warn-only; enabled enforce for internal routes. Rejection rate ~6% initially, mostly missing baseline for quant routes and out-of-range microbatch tokens. Adjusted recommender to stop emitting those; now ~1.1%.
